features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_localized_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment cite a specific, localized example (a particular named or concretely situated case, place, event, person or instance) as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. Output 1 if at least one comment offers a specific, localized example as support for its counter-argument: a concrete, particular case tied to an identifiable place, event, person, organization, time or situation (e.g., a named country's policy, a particular incident, a specific personal experience in a described setting). Generic, abstract, hypothetical or purely general-category examples do not count. A quoted or cited external example counts if used as support in the comment. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output 0 if no comment qualifies or the list is validly empty. Output null if OC_comments is missing or cannot be parsed. Presence only, not a count.

h0: any_comment_cites_specific_localized_example has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_specific_localized_example = 1 have a higher probability of the OP changing their view than those with 0.
note: Presence interpretation (at least one qualifying comment) since no quantity specified. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only, not causal. Comments are current text; OC_comments may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt is told to disregard as evidence. "Specific, localized" operationalized as concrete particular case tied to identifiable place/event/person/situation; judged from comment text alone.
